races.title: State Senate, District 21
races.note: Special election to fill the rest of this Senate term (Division of Elections election 20261103-S01).

cands.name: Jordan Hensley
cands.bio: Democratic political newcomer; works as a bartender at the Fenway Hotel in Dunedin. Says he entered the race because no Democrat filed against Nocco. No prior political office.
cands.local_ties: Works in Dunedin (Pinellas). Says he and his wife live paycheck to paycheck. DOE filing county is Pasco; home city not stated. SD 21 covers northern Pinellas and southwest Pasco.

money_notes.text: Says he has raised about $10,000 (Tampa Bay 28 report).

endorsements.text: Creative Loafing Tampa Bay recommends Hensley. Tampa Bay 28 reports no formal endorsements; co-workers at the Fenway have backed him.

cands.gaps: Social links and photo not found. Owner-source search not run (search budget exhausted).

cands.name: Chris Nocco
cands.bio: Republican; Pasco County Sheriff since April 2011 (appointed by Gov. Rick Scott, elected 2012, unopposed 2016, 2020, 2024). Former Marco Rubio staffer; appointed to the Homeland Security Advisory Council by President Trump in 2020. Running for the seat Sen. Ed Hooper is leaving.
cands.local_ties: Pasco County Sheriff for 15 years. FL DOE shows a filing address county code of LEO (Leon), which does not match Pasco; likely a campaign mailing address, not verified. SD 21 covers northern Pinellas and southwest Pasco.

record.text: Sheriff's office budget more than doubled under him, to about $174.5 million; he will remain sheriff until the November election and Gov. DeSantis would appoint a successor.
2015 body cameras for patrol deputies; 2016 #9PMROUTINE campaign.

money_notes.text: Campaign finance records show he raised more than $260,000 (Tampa Bay 28).

controversies.text: A 2020 Tampa Bay Times investigation reported a sheriff's program that sent deputies repeatedly to families' homes, including children's. In a December 2024 settlement, his office acknowledged it interfered with four residents' constitutional rights, ended the program and agreed to pay $105,000. The office said it settled to save taxpayers money and won't apologize.

endorsements.text: Gov. Ron DeSantis and other Republican leaders (Tampa Bay 28).

cands.gaps: Photo not found (no Wikipedia page for the person). Residence not stated. Owner-source search not run (search budget exhausted). Wikipedia says Hooper is 'resigning Nov 3, 2026'; reason for leaving not verified.
